The saturation screen was not consulted because the hold concerned linework legibility, not colour saturation.

The hold's specific claims fail:

1. "Tile 2 has no contour stroke at all" (P7000527, seed 2002) is false. At 4x on the shoulder (crop 100,700-300,860) there is an unmistakable garment stroke that begins in a heavy pressure node at the shoulder point, runs down-right with a thick belly, and tapers to a fine hairline tail — textbook elastic-pressure entry-swell/exit-taper. At 4x on the neckline (crop 400,580-720,720) a dark contour follows the underside of the crew collar band, modulating from a near-invisible hairline where it exits right, through moderate weight along the curve, into a distinctly heavier stroke at the left shoulder. A soft dry-brush silhouette contour also separates the left arm from the background.

2. "Only a single lapel/placket line" in tiles 1 and 3 is an undercount. P7000526 carries the lapel roll edge, the notch (heavy), the placket running from notch to hem with a clear thin→thick→thin progression, a fully drawn button ring whose stroke is heavy at the bottom and thin at the top, plus a light tapered flap stroke on the wearer's right. P7000528 carries the collar edge, lapel roll, notch corner, placket, and a fine sleeve/shoulder seam hairline, contrasting fine hairlines against heavy notch strokes.

3. Quantitatively, the three seeds are indistinguishable in line content, so tile 2 is not an outlier: dark-line pixel fraction 0.0049 / 0.0047 / 0.0048, with scanline run widths spanning p10=1px to max 25 / 19 / 24px. That ~20x spread between hairline and belly is the weight modulation elastic_pressure encodes, and it is far larger than any 256px downscale could preserve — which is exactly why the contact sheet flattened it into "no stroke".

elastic_pressure is readable and separable at full resolution across all three seeds; warm_earth (olive/khaki) and broad_blended_plane were already conceded as clear. No defect.
